questions.title: 60 m away, 45° elevation: height?
questions.text: A point on the ground is 60 m away from the foot of a vertical tower. If the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from that point is 45°, then the height of the tower (in m) is:
steps: ① Draw: tower TF (height h), point P on the ground
② PF = 60 m, angle at P = 45°
③ Height and distance ⟹ use tan
questions.trap: Using sin 45° here. You know the ground distance, not the slant line, so use tan.
questions.tryit: A tower is 50 m high. From a point on the ground the elevation of its top is 45°. How far is the point?

questions.title: 30 m tower, car 10√3 m away: angle?
questions.text: A car is moving away from the base of a 30 m high tower. The angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the car, when the car is 10√3 m away from the base of the tower, is:
steps: ① Draw: tower TF = 30 m, car C on the ground
② CF = 10√3 m, angle at C = θ
⑤ Which angle has tan = √3?  tan 60° = √3
questions.trap: Simplifying 3/√3 to 1/√3. Multiply top and bottom by √3: 3/√3 = √3.
questions.tryit: A 15 m pole casts a shadow 15√3 m long. Find the Sun's elevation.

questions.title: Kite string 52 m, tan θ = 12/5: height?
questions.text: The string of a kite is 52 m long. If the string makes an angle θ with the ground such that tan θ = 12/5, the height of the kite above the ground is:
steps: ① Draw: string OK = 52 m (the slant side), angle θ at O
questions.remember: 5, 12, 13 is a Pythagorean triple. tan = 12/5 ⟹ sin = 12/13.
questions.trap: Taking the string as the ground distance. The string is the slant side, the hypotenuse.
questions.tryit: A 20 m ladder makes an angle θ with the ground where sin θ = 3/5. How high does it reach?

questions.title: Case study: Tejas and the moving car
questions.text:
Tejas is standing on the top of a building. He sees a car moving towards the building at an angle of depression of 30°. After 6 seconds, the angle of depression becomes 60°, and the car is then 25 m away from the building.
(i) Find the height of the building.  (ii) Find the distance travelled by the car in those 6 seconds.
(iii) How long will the car take from its first position to reach the foot of the building?
steps: ① Depression angle at the top = elevation angle at the car
④ Distance travelled = 75 − 25 = 50 m in 6 s
questions.remember: Angle of depression from the top = angle of elevation from the ground (alternate angles).
questions.trap: Putting the depression angle inside the triangle at the top. Move it down to the car: it's the same angle there.
questions.tryit: In the same story, how far is Tejas from the car (straight line) when the angle is 60°?

questions.title: Kite 60 m high, seen from a roof and from the ground (5 marks)
questions.text: A kite is flying at a height of 60 m above the ground level. Ravi, standing at the roof of the house, is holding the string straight and observes the angle of elevation of the kite as 30°. From the bottom of the same building, the angle of elevation of the kite is 45°. Find the length of the string and the height of the roof from the ground. (Use √3 = 1.73)
steps: ① Draw: kite K at 60 m · roof height h · horizontal distance d
② From the bottom (45°): tan 45° = 60 / d ⟹ d = 60 m
③ From the roof, the kite is only (60 − h) m higher
⑥ String L is the slant side: sin 30° = (60 − h) / L
questions.remember: Two observers ⟹ two right triangles that share a side. Solve the easy one (45°) first.
questions.trap: Measuring the 30° triangle from the ground. From the roof, the kite is only (60 − h) metres higher.
questions.tryit: A kite is 60 m high and its string makes 60° with the ground. Find the string length.

questions.title: Manish's kite, seen by Mahesh from a 50 m roof (5 marks)
questions.text: Manish is flying a kite with a 200 m long string, which makes an angle of elevation of 30° with the ground. Mahesh is on the roof of a 50 m high building on the opposite side, and sees the same kite at an angle of elevation of 45°. Find the distance between the kite and Mahesh.
steps: ① Draw: string MK = 200 m at 30° · Mahesh on a 50 m roof
② Kite height: sin 30° = KG / 200 ⟹ KG = 200 × 1/2 = 100 m
④ Mahesh → kite is the slant side at 45°
questions.remember: Slant side known or wanted ⟹ use sin (or cos). Only flat distances ⟹ use tan.
questions.trap: Forgetting to subtract the 50 m roof. Mahesh sees only the part of the height above his eyes.
questions.tryit: From a 60 m roof, a kite at 120 m is seen at 30° elevation. How far is the kite (straight line)?
